item.vignette: An 8-year-old girl has progressive ataxia, dysarthria, vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, and splenomegaly. Cultured skin fibroblasts show intense perinuclear filipin staining caused by lysosomal accumulation of unesterified cholesterol.
item.lead_in: Which cellular process is most directly impaired in this disorder?

options.A: Intracellular trafficking of unesterified cholesterol and other lipid cargo out of late endosomal-lysosomal compartments by NPC1/NPC2
options.B: Lysosomal hydrolysis of sphingomyelin by acid sphingomyelinase
options.C: Receptor-mediated endocytosis of circulating LDL through the LDL receptor
options.D: Esterification of free cholesterol in the endoplasmic reticulum by acyl-CoA:cholesterol acyltransferase
options.E: Peroxisomal beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids

item.tested_construct: Loss of NPC1/NPC2 function causing lysosomal accumulation of unesterified cholesterol and other lipid cargo
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Niemann-Pick disease type C is caused by loss of NPC1 or NPC2 function. These proteins are involved in intracellular cholesterol handling; their deficiency causes lysosomal accumulation of lipid cargo, including unesterified cholesterol. The neurologic-visceral phenotype plus filipin-positive lysosomal cholesterol accumulation therefore points to defective NPC1/NPC2-dependent lipid trafficking.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. Loss of NPC1 or NPC2 function causes accumulation of unesterified cholesterol and other lipid cargo in lysosomes, reflecting impaired intracellular lipid trafficking.
distractor_explanations.B: Acid sphingomyelinase deficiency causes acid sphingomyelinase deficiency disease with sphingomyelin accumulation, not the characteristic NPC lysosomal unesterified-cholesterol trafficking defect.
distractor_explanations.C: LDL-receptor deficiency impairs plasma LDL clearance and causes hypercholesterolemia; it does not produce the characteristic NPC neurovisceral phenotype with lysosomal filipin-positive cholesterol accumulation.
distractor_explanations.D: ACAT-mediated cholesterol esterification occurs in the endoplasmic reticulum and is not the primary defect in NPC1/NPC2 deficiency.
distractor_explanations.E: Defective peroxisomal beta-oxidation causes accumulation of very-long-chain fatty acids rather than the NPC pattern of lysosomal unesterified-cholesterol accumulation.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize Niemann-Pick disease type C as an NPC1/NPC2 loss-of-function disorder in which defective intracellular lipid trafficking produces lysosomal accumulation of unesterified cholesterol and other lipid cargo.

item.vignette: A 3-year-old boy has recurrent severe bacterial infections without pus formation, persistent leukocytosis, gingival bleeding, and recurrent epistaxis. Flow cytometry shows normal surface expression of beta2 integrins on leukocytes and alpha-IIb-beta3 integrin on platelets, but receptor stimulation fails to induce high-affinity ligand binding in either cell type.
item.lead_in: Which molecular defect best explains both the immune and bleeding manifestations?

options.A: Loss of the beta2-integrin subunit CD18, preventing leukocyte integrin surface expression
options.B: Loss of FERMT3-encoded kindlin-3, impairing inside-out activation of hematopoietic-cell integrins
options.C: Loss of platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa expression with otherwise normal leukocyte integrin activation
options.D: Defective phagocyte NADPH oxidase assembly, preventing the respiratory burst
options.E: Loss of the Golgi GDP-fucose transporter SLC35C1, impairing selectin-ligand fucosylation and leukocyte rolling

item.tested_construct: FERMT3/kindlin-3 deficiency causing defective inside-out integrin activation in leukocytes and platelets
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type III is caused by FERMT3 mutations that reduce or eliminate kindlin-3. Leukocytes and platelets can retain beta1, beta2, and beta3 integrin expression, but defective inside-out signaling prevents normal integrin activation. Because the defect affects hematopoietic-cell integrins in both leukocytes and platelets, patients develop recurrent infections together with a Glanzmann-like bleeding phenotype.

distractor_explanations.A: CD18 deficiency causes LAD-I with absent or markedly reduced beta2-integrin surface expression; this patient has normal beta2-integrin expression but defective activation.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. FERMT3 encodes kindlin-3, which is required for inside-out activation of hematopoietic-cell integrins; deficiency affects both leukocyte adhesion and platelet function.
distractor_explanations.C: Loss of platelet alpha-IIb-beta3 causes Glanzmann thrombasthenia and bleeding but does not explain defective leukocyte integrin activation and recurrent infections.
distractor_explanations.D: NADPH oxidase deficiency impairs intracellular killing after phagocytosis; it does not cause the combined leukocyte-and-platelet integrin activation defect.
distractor_explanations.E: SLC35C1 deficiency causes LAD-II by impairing fucosylation of selectin ligands and leukocyte rolling; it does not cause the combined leukocyte-and-platelet inside-out integrin activation defect.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish LAD-III from LAD-I and isolated platelet disorders by recognizing normal integrin surface expression with defective FERMT3/kindlin-3-dependent inside-out activation in both leukocytes and platelets.

item.vignette: A 9-year-old boy has epilepsy beginning in infancy, nonprogressive cerebellar ataxia, sensorineural hearing loss, and chronic salt wasting. Laboratory studies show hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypomagnesemia, and low urinary calcium.
item.lead_in: Which renal transport abnormality most directly accounts for the salt-wasting tubulopathy?

options.A: Loss of apical NKCC2-mediated sodium-potassium-chloride uptake in the thick ascending limb
options.B: Loss of apical ROMK-mediated potassium recycling in the thick ascending limb
options.C: Reduced basolateral potassium conductance through Kir4.1 in distal convoluted tubular cells, impairing salt reabsorption
options.D: Constitutive activation of epithelial sodium channels in principal cells of the collecting duct
options.E: Loss of apical pendrin-mediated chloride-bicarbonate exchange in beta-intercalated cells

item.tested_construct: KCNJ10/Kir4.1 loss reduces basolateral potassium conductance in distal convoluted tubular cells and impairs renal salt reabsorption
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: KCNJ10 encodes the inwardly rectifying potassium channel Kir4.1. In kidney, KCNJ10 localizes to basolateral membranes of distal tubular segments, especially the distal convoluted tubule. EAST/SeSAME-associated loss-of-function variants markedly reduce channel activity, disrupting the basolateral potassium conductance needed for efficient distal salt transport and producing a Gitelman-like salt-wasting tubulopathy.

distractor_explanations.A: NKCC2 loss causes Bartter syndrome, which localizes primarily to the thick ascending limb and does not explain the neurologic and auditory syndrome caused by KCNJ10 variants.
distractor_explanations.B: ROMK loss causes a form of Bartter syndrome; KCNJ10 instead encodes the basolateral Kir4.1 channel in distal tubular cells.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. KCNJ10 loss impairs basolateral Kir4.1 potassium-channel function in distal convoluted tubular cells, reducing the transport capacity that supports salt reabsorption.
distractor_explanations.D: ENaC activation causes sodium retention, hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis rather than renal salt wasting with the EAST neurologic phenotype.
distractor_explanations.E: Pendrin loss causes a different chloride-handling disorder and does not explain the characteristic KCNJ10-associated neurologic, auditory, and distal-tubular phenotype.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize EAST/SeSAME syndrome as KCNJ10/Kir4.1 loss of function and connect the renal phenotype to impaired basolateral potassium conductance in distal convoluted tubular cells.

item.vignette: A 24-year-old woman has lifelong compensated hemolysis, splenomegaly, and dehydrated erythrocytes with increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration. Her father has similar findings. Sequencing identifies a gain-of-function variant in PIEZO1 that prolongs activity of the mechanically activated cation channel.
item.lead_in: Which downstream ionic sequence most directly causes erythrocyte dehydration in this disorder?

options.A: Reduced calcium entry followed by inhibition of potassium efflux through the Gardos channel
options.B: Increased sodium entry followed by osmotic water influx through aquaporin-1
options.C: Increased chloride entry followed by activation of the erythrocyte sodium-potassium ATPase
options.D: Increased calcium entry followed by activation of the KCa3.1 Gardos channel and loss of potassium and water
options.E: Reduced proton extrusion followed by intracellular alkalinization and water loss

item.tested_construct: PIEZO1-mediated calcium entry activates the KCa3.1 Gardos channel, promoting potassium loss and erythrocyte dehydration
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: PIEZO1 is a mechanically activated cation channel involved in erythrocyte volume regulation. Excess PIEZO1 activity increases calcium entry. The rise in intracellular calcium activates the calcium-sensitive KCa3.1 Gardos channel, driving potassium efflux; water follows osmotically, producing the dehydrated erythrocyte phenotype of hereditary xerocytosis/dehydrated hereditary stomatocytosis.

distractor_explanations.A: The pathogenic sequence begins with increased, not reduced, calcium entry; Gardos-channel activation promotes rather than inhibits potassium loss.
distractor_explanations.B: Sustained sodium and water influx would tend to swell erythrocytes rather than produce the characteristic dehydration.
distractor_explanations.C: The experimentally demonstrated downstream effector of PIEZO1-mediated calcium entry is the KCa3.1 Gardos potassium channel, not a chloride-triggered increase in sodium-potassium ATPase activity.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. Increased PIEZO1-dependent calcium entry activates KCa3.1/Gardos channels, leading to potassium efflux and osmotic water loss from erythrocytes.
distractor_explanations.E: Intracellular alkalinization is not the defining downstream mechanism linking PIEZO1 gain of function to erythrocyte dehydration.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect PIEZO1 gain of function in hereditary xerocytosis to calcium influx, secondary KCa3.1/Gardos-channel activation, potassium efflux, and osmotic water loss.

item.vignette: A 2-year-old boy is evaluated after recurrent fasting hypoglycemia and seizures. He has diffuse hyperpigmentation. Morning cortisol is very low and plasma ACTH is markedly elevated, but serum sodium, potassium, plasma renin activity, and aldosterone are normal. Sequencing shows no pathogenic variant in the coding region of MC2R. In cultured adrenal cells, the ACTH receptor is synthesized but fails to reach the plasma membrane.
item.lead_in: Which protein defect most directly explains these findings?

options.A: Loss of steroidogenic acute regulatory protein, preventing mitochondrial cholesterol transport
options.B: Loss of 21-hydroxylase, impairing cortisol and aldosterone synthesis
options.C: Activating mutation of the calcium-sensing receptor, suppressing parathyroid hormone release
options.D: Loss of the glucocorticoid receptor, causing peripheral cortisol resistance
options.E: Loss of MRAP, preventing normal trafficking of the melanocortin-2 ACTH receptor to the cell surface

item.tested_construct: MRAP deficiency preventing trafficking of MC2R/ACTH receptor to the adrenal-cell surface
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Familial glucocorticoid deficiency can result from defects in MRAP, the melanocortin-2 receptor accessory protein. MRAP is required for trafficking MC2R, the ACTH receptor, to the cell surface. Failure of this step produces ACTH resistance with very low cortisol and compensatory ACTH elevation while mineralocorticoid function can remain preserved.

distractor_explanations.A: StAR deficiency causes lipoid congenital adrenal hyperplasia with broad adrenal and gonadal steroid deficiency rather than isolated ACTH resistance with preserved mineralocorticoid function.
distractor_explanations.B: 21-hydroxylase deficiency impairs both cortisol synthesis and, in classic salt-wasting disease, mineralocorticoid synthesis; it does not specifically prevent MC2R surface trafficking.
distractor_explanations.C: Calcium-sensing receptor activation causes hypocalcemia with low or inappropriately normal parathyroid hormone and does not explain ACTH resistance.
distractor_explanations.D: Glucocorticoid-receptor resistance generally produces elevated cortisol as well as elevated ACTH, rather than severe cortisol deficiency from failure of adrenal ACTH signaling.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. MRAP is an accessory protein essential for trafficking MC2R to the cell surface; loss causes familial glucocorticoid deficiency with ACTH resistance.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize MRAP as the accessory protein required for MC2R/ACTH-receptor surface trafficking and link its loss to familial glucocorticoid deficiency with preserved mineralocorticoid function.
